title: Governed estate resource assignment and its attestation
description: ADR-SHARED-042 section 14, Decision 9 (Platform Owner, 23 October 2026): the Control Plane establishes the Digital Estate provenance of a native commitment that does not arrive through a governed BFF. A BFF commitment's estate is proven by the CP estate-client binding (estate-client-binding.schema.json); a non-BFF commitment's estate is proven only by an ACTIVE, approved EstateResourceAssignment, attested by CP for one request. Two scopes exist. WORKLOAD assigns an authenticated server application (identified by its own IAM workload identity, never a Medusa publishable or secret key) to one estate. NATIVE_RESOURCE assigns one Trade native seller configuration (the reference and digest Trade has attested to CP under Trade-0) to one estate, for native operations, background jobs, callbacks and replays; Trade establishes which native configuration a resource belongs to from its own server-read records, never from caller input. An API key, sales channel, publishable key, domain or caller-asserted estate is never provenance. An assignment classifies nothing (the estate commerce profile does), authorises no seller, buyer, market or purchasing action, and is never inferred: it is proposed, independently approved (four-eyes), revisioned, and suspended or revoked through the governed lifecycle below. Both provenances converge on the same estate commerce profile attestation and the same universal native commit fence. This contract registers no assignment and allocates no scope.

assignmentScope.description: WORKLOAD: an authenticated server application, by its IAM workload client id. NATIVE_RESOURCE: one Trade native seller configuration, by its Trade-0 reference and digest.

assignmentStatus.description: PROPOSED is never attested. Only ACTIVE inside its effective interval is attested. SUSPENDED returns to ACTIVE only through an approved reinstatement; REVOKED is terminal.

permittedOperation.description: The native commitment operations (trade/v2 order-operations.yaml; Decision 6) the assignment establishes estate provenance for. Nothing else.

evidenceReference.description: Redacted, auditable provenance (for example a change-set or approval-decision id). Never a credential or unnecessary personal data.

workloadClientId.description: The IAM workload client id of an authenticated server application.

nativeResource.description: A Trade native seller configuration exactly as Trade attested it to CP (trade/v2 seller-operating-binding.schema.json, Trade-0). CP verifies it against its own record of that attestation for the calling engine instance.

EstateResourceAssignment.description: The governed record. CP owns its lifecycle: the scope, subject, estate, Tenant, engine instance, Markets and operations are immutable (a change is a new assignment), the revision is CP-controlled and increases by one on every change, the approver is never the proposer, and nothing is deleted. At most one ACTIVE assignment covers a subject, engine instance, Market and operation at a time.

proposed_by.description: The canonical human Principal who proposed it.

approved_by.description: The canonical human Principal who approved it; never proposed_by.

allOf.description: A WORKLOAD assignment names the workload and no native resource; a NATIVE_RESOURCE assignment the reverse.
Anything that has ever been attestable carries its approval.

EstateResourceAssignmentProposal.description: Propose an assignment (PROPOSED, revision 1). The proposer is the authenticated human caller, never a field.

EstateResourceAssignmentTransition.description: A governed lifecycle change, applied only to the stated current revision. APPROVE (PROPOSED to ACTIVE) and REINSTATE (SUSPENDED to ACTIVE) require a human who is not the proposer; SUSPEND and REVOKE take effect immediately and stop attestation. The Tenant is derived by CP from the estate, never supplied.

EstateResourceAssignmentResolveRequest.description: The calling Trade workload asks whether one native commitment operation, on its own engine instance and in a Market, has governed estate provenance. For WORKLOAD it presents the server application's own IAM workload token as evidence, which CP verifies and introspects itself; for NATIVE_RESOURCE it names the native configuration Trade itself resolved for the resource. It cannot name a Tenant, assignment or revision.

workload_evidence.description: WORKLOAD only: the server application's IAM workload access token for audience baobab-trade with scope trade:native-commitment:submit. Never echoed or logged.

EstateResourceAssignmentAttestation.description: CP's attestation that exactly one ACTIVE, approved, currently effective assignment gives the operation estate provenance. expires_at is at most 60 seconds after issued_at and never later than the assignment's effective_until (carried when present). Its attestation_id is the GOVERNED_RESOURCE_ASSIGNMENT reference a Trade workload presents to resolveEstateCommerceProfile, which CP re-verifies from its own record. It is provenance only.

EstateResourceAssignmentDenialCode.description: Closed problem codes (errors/v1 problem-details code). Every denial is fail-closed and discloses no other estate, Tenant or assignment. WORKLOAD_EVIDENCE_INVALID: the server application's token does not verify, is not current, or lacks trade:native-commitment:submit. NATIVE_RESOURCE_NOT_ATTESTED: CP holds no current Trade-0 attestation of that native configuration for the calling instance. ASSIGNMENT_NOT_FOUND: no assignment covers the subject and estate. ASSIGNMENT_NOT_ACTIVE: the only match is PROPOSED, SUSPENDED, REVOKED or outside its interval. OPERATION_NOT_PERMITTED, MARKET_NOT_PERMITTED, ENGINE_INSTANCE_NOT_PERMITTED: the match does not cover it. ASSIGNMENT_AMBIGUOUS: more than one applies; nothing is attested. RESOLUTION_UNAVAILABLE: never a fallback.
